hook_text: Three cells, one bulb, two ways to connect them. One way doubles the brightness. The other triples the hours. Here is which is which.
clip_script: A cell is two different electrodes in a conducting paste; chemistry fixes its volts at about 1.5, and size sets how long it lasts, its capacity. Series, end to end: volts add, three cells 4.5 volts, but capacity stays at one cell's, and one weak or reversed cell spoils the stack. Three in series on a 3 volt bulb? Brilliant, then dead. Parallel, side by side: volts stay 1.5, capacity triples, perfect for lasting all night, but the cells must match or the fresh one cooks the tired one. Ask two questions: what volts does it need, how long must it run.
visual_style: Whiteboard cell cutaway; cells line up end to end and a voltmeter climbs; cells line up side by side and an hourglass grows; a 3 volt bulb flares and dies; an electric car pack shows both patterns.
pacing: Cell, series, bench burnout, parallel, choosing.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and measure two cells in series and in parallel with a multimeter.
